summary.en: A trading kingdom of the northern Ethiopian highlands and Eritrea, Aksum controlled Red Sea commerce through the port of Adulis, minted gold coins and raised monumental stelae. Christian from the 4th century, it was counted by the Persian prophet Mani among the four great kingdoms of the world.
summary.zh: 阿克苏姆是埃塞俄比亚北部高原和厄立特里亚的贸易王国，经阿杜利斯港控制红海贸易，铸造金币并竖立巨型石碑。自4世纪起信奉基督教，被波斯先知摩尼列为世界四大王国之一。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Aksum
S. Munro-Hay, Aksum: An African Civilisation of Late Antiquity (1991)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Aksum
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. II: Ancient Civilizations of Africa (ed. G. Mokhtar, 1981)

note: Wikidata dates proto-Aksumite beginnings to c. 400 BCE; the kingdom proper is usually dated from the 1st century CE. End date (c. 940–960) is uncertain. Reign dates are approximate.

summary.en: The largest of the Christian Nubian kingdoms on the middle Nile, Makuria absorbed Nobadia, held off the Arabs under the Baqt treaty, and produced the painted cathedral of Faras. Mamluk interventions from the 1270s and Arab migration led to its fragmentation.
summary.zh: 马库里亚是尼罗河中游最大的基督教努比亚王国，兼并诺巴迪亚，凭巴克特条约抵御阿拉伯人，留下法拉斯大教堂壁画。13世纪70年代起马穆鲁克的干预和阿拉伯部落迁入使其分崩离析。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Makuria
Derek A. Welsby, The Medieval Kingdoms of Nubia (2002)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. III: Africa from the Seventh to the Eleventh Century (ed. M. El Fasi & I. Hrbek, 1988)

note: Origins (6th century) and end (records fade after c. 1400; Wikidata 1518) are approximate, as are reign dates.

capital.zh: 开罗（973年起；此前为拉卡达与马赫迪耶）

summary.en: An Ismaʿili Shiʿi caliphate proclaimed in Ifriqiya by ʿAbdallah al-Mahdi, the Fatimids conquered Egypt in 969 and founded Cairo. At its height it ruled North Africa, Sicily, Syria and the Hejaz and fostered al-Azhar and the Red Sea trade, before Saladin ended it in 1171.
summary.zh: 法蒂玛王朝是阿卜杜拉·马赫迪在伊弗里基叶宣告建立的伊斯玛仪派什叶派哈里发国，969年征服埃及并建开罗。鼎盛时统治北非、西西里、叙利亚和汉志，扶植爱资哈尔与红海贸易，1171年为萨拉丁所终结。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Fatimid Caliphate
Michael Brett, The Fatimid Empire (2017)
Britannica: Fāṭimid dynasty

summary.en: Ruled by sultans drawn from a self-renewing elite of military slaves of Turkic and later Circassian origin, the Mamluk state defeated the Mongols at ʿAyn Jalut (1260), expelled the Crusaders and made Cairo the leading city of the Islamic world until the Ottoman conquest.
summary.zh: 马穆鲁克王朝的苏丹出自不断更新的军事奴隶精英，先为突厥裔，后为切尔克斯裔。王朝于1260年在阿音扎鲁特击败蒙古人，驱逐十字军，使开罗成为伊斯兰世界首要城市，直至奥斯曼征服。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mamluk Sultanate
Robert Irwin, The Middle East in the Middle Ages: The Early Mamluk Sultanate 1250–1382 (1986)
Britannica: Mamluk

note: al-Nasir Muhammad reigned three times (1293–94, 1299–1309, 1310–41).

summary.en: The Soninke kingdom of Wagadu, whose ruler’s title “ghana” Arab writers used for the state, grew rich taxing the trans-Saharan gold and salt trade. Al-Bakri described its twin-town capital in 1068; it declined after Almoravid pressure and was absorbed by Mali in the 13th century.
summary.zh: 索宁克人的瓦加杜王国因国王称号“加纳”而被阿拉伯作家以此称之，依靠对跨撒哈拉黄金与食盐贸易征税而致富。巴克里于1068年记述了其双城式都城；王国在穆拉比特的压力下衰落，13世纪并入马里。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ghana Empire
al-Bakri, Kitab al-Masalik wa'l-Mamalik (1068), in Levtzion & Hopkins, Corpus
Nehemia Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. III: Africa from the Seventh to the Eleventh Century (ed. M. El Fasi & I. Hrbek, 1988)

note: Origins are unknown (Wikidata: c. 100 CE; often given as 3rd–4th century). The nature and date of the Almoravid “conquest” (1076) are debated.

capital.zh: 尼亚尼（传统说法，位置有争议）

summary.en: Founded by Sundiata Keita, Mali controlled the goldfields of Bambuk and Bure and the Sahelian trade cities, stretching from the Atlantic to beyond the Niger bend. Under Mansa Musa and Mansa Sulayman it was among the wealthiest states in the world; it contracted after the rise of Songhai.
summary.zh: 马里帝国由松迪亚塔·凯塔创建，控制班布克和布雷金矿及萨赫勒商业城市，疆域从大西洋延伸至尼日尔河湾以东。在曼萨·穆萨和曼萨·苏莱曼时期跻身世界最富有的国家之列；桑海崛起后逐渐收缩。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mali Empire
Nehemia Levtzion, Ancient Ghana and Mali (1973)
N. Levtzion & J. F. P. Hopkins (eds.), Corpus of Early Arabic Sources for West African History (1981)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. IV: Africa from the Twelfth to the Sixteenth Century (ed. D. T. Niane, 1984)

note: Reign dates follow Ibn Khaldun’s chronology and are approximate.

summary.en: From Gao on the Niger, Sonni Ali conquered Timbuktu and Djenné, and the Askia dynasty built the largest empire in West African history, with a professional army, river fleet and provincial governors. It collapsed after the Moroccan victory at Tondibi.
summary.zh: 索尼·阿里以尼日尔河畔的加奥为中心征服廷巴克图与杰内，阿斯基亚王朝建立了西非历史上最大的帝国，拥有职业军队、河上舰队和行省总督。汤迪比之战摩洛哥获胜后帝国崩溃。

name.zh: 阿斯基亚·穆罕默德一世
阿斯基亚·伊斯哈格二世

sources.title: Wikipedia: Songhai Empire
al-Sa'di, Tarikh al-Sudan (c. 1655), trans. J. O. Hunwick, Timbuktu and the Songhay Empire (2003)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Tomb of Askia
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. IV: Africa from the Twelfth to the Sixteenth Century (ed. D. T. Niane, 1984)

capital.zh: 恩吉米（加涅姆）；恩加扎尔加穆（博尔努，约1470年起）

summary.en: One of Africa’s longest-lived states, ruled for about a millennium by the Sayfawa dynasty around Lake Chad. Its kings converted to Islam in the 11th century; driven west of the lake to Bornu in the 14th, it revived under Idris Alooma, whose musketeers dominated the central Sudan.
summary.zh: 加涅姆-博尔努是非洲存续最久的国家之一，赛法瓦王朝在乍得湖周围统治约一千年。其国王于11世纪皈依伊斯兰教；14世纪被迫迁至湖西的博尔努，在伊德里斯·阿卢马时期复兴，其火枪队称雄中苏丹。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kanem–Bornu Empire
Dierk Lange, Le Dīwān des sultans du [Kānem-]Bornū (1977)
Ahmad ibn Furtu, Kitab ghazawat Barnu (1576)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. IV: Africa from the Twelfth to the Sixteenth Century (ed. D. T. Niane, 1984)

note: Start date is traditional (Wikidata gives c. 11th century, when the Sayfawa converted); reign dates vary between chronologies. al-Kanemi was de facto ruler, not Sayfawa king. Capital coordinates are those of Ngazargamu.

summary.en: An Agaw dynasty that ruled the Ethiopian highlands between the decline of Aksum and the Solomonic restoration. Its kings sponsored the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and kept ties with the Coptic Church of Egypt; Yekuno Amlak overthrew it in 1270.
summary.zh: 扎格维王朝是阿高人王朝，统治埃塞俄比亚高原于阿克苏姆衰落与所罗门王朝复辟之间。其国王营建拉利贝拉岩石教堂，并与埃及科普特教会保持联系；1270年被耶库诺·阿姆拉克推翻。

name.zh: 耶姆雷哈纳·克里斯托斯
盖布雷·梅斯克尔·拉利贝拉

sources.title: Wikipedia: Zagwe dynasty
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)
Taddesse Tamrat, Church and State in Ethiopia 1270–1527 (1972)

note: Start date disputed: Wikidata gives c. 900; many historians favour c. 1137. Lalibela’s reign dates approximate.

summary.en: A Shona state of the Zimbabwe plateau that succeeded Mapungubwe, with Great Zimbabwe as its royal centre. It controlled gold exports to the Swahili coast; when it declined in the 15th century, power passed north to Mutapa and west to Butua (Torwa).
summary.zh: 津巴布韦王国是承接马蓬古布韦的津巴布韦高原绍纳人国家，以大津巴布韦为王都，控制向斯瓦希里海岸出口黄金。15世纪衰落后，权力北移至穆塔帕，西移至布图阿（托尔瓦）。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Great Zimbabwe
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Great Zimbabwe National Monument
Innocent Pikirayi, The Zimbabwe Culture (2001)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. IV: Africa from the Twelfth to the Sixteenth Century (ed. D. T. Niane, 1984)

note: No rulers are known by name; dates are archaeological.

capital.en: Zvongombe and later sites in the Dande and Mount Fura area
capital.zh: 兹冯贡贝及丹德—富拉山一带的后续王都

summary.en: Founded by Nyatsimba Mutota, the Mutapa state dominated the northern Zimbabwe plateau and Zambezi trade. The Portuguese, who called it Monomotapa, sought its gold; after defeat in 1629 the mwenemutapa became a Portuguese vassal, and the kingdom gradually lost ground to the Rozvi.
summary.zh: 穆塔帕王国由尼亚特辛巴·穆托塔创建，主宰津巴布韦高原北部和赞比西河贸易。葡萄牙人称之为“莫诺莫塔帕”并觊觎其黄金；1629年战败后穆塔帕王沦为葡萄牙附庸，王国逐渐让位于罗兹维。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mutapa Empire
S. I. G. Mudenge, A Political History of Munhumutapa c. 1400–1902 (1988)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. V: Africa from the Sixteenth to the Eighteenth Century (ed. B. A. Ogot, 1992)

note: Capital sites shifted; coordinates mark the Mount Fura (Mount Darwin) area approximately. Wikidata’s coordinates fall at Great Zimbabwe.

capital.zh: 姆班扎刚果（圣萨尔瓦多）

summary.en: A centralised kingdom south of the lower Congo River, Kongo adopted Catholicism after contact with Portugal in 1483 and exchanged ambassadors with Lisbon and the Vatican. The Atlantic slave trade and defeat at Mbwila in 1665 brought civil war; it became a Portuguese vassal in the later 19th century, and Portugal abolished the titular monarchy in 1914.
summary.zh: 刚果王国是刚果河下游以南的中央集权王国，1483年与葡萄牙接触后接受天主教，并与里斯本和梵蒂冈互派使节。大西洋奴隶贸易及1665年姆布维拉之败导致内战；19世纪后期沦为葡萄牙附庸，1914年葡萄牙废除其名义上的王位。

name.zh: 恩津加·恩库武（若昂一世）
阿方索一世（姆文巴·恩津加）

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kongo
John K. Thornton, A History of West Central Africa to 1850 (2020)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Mbanza Kongo, Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. V: Africa from the Sixteenth to the Eighteenth Century (ed. B. A. Ogot, 1992)
Britannica: Kongo

note: End is 1914, when Portugal abolished the titular monarchy after suppressing the 1913–14 revolt; Wikidata gives 1888, the year of formal Portuguese vassalage. Founding date approximate.

name.zh: 埃塞俄比亚帝国（所罗门王朝）

capital.en: Mobile royal camps; Gondar (1636–1855); Addis Ababa (from 1886)
capital.zh: 流动王营；贡德尔（1636–1855）；亚的斯亚贝巴（1886年起）

summary.en: Claiming descent from Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, the Solomonic dynasty ruled the Christian highlands for seven centuries, surviving the Adal war, the Era of the Princes and Italian invasions. Under Menelik II it expanded to near its modern size; the Derg abolished the monarchy in 1974–75.
summary.zh: 所罗门王朝自称所罗门与示巴女王的后裔，统治基督教高原七个世纪，历经阿达尔战争、王子纷争时代和意大利入侵而延续。孟尼利克二世时扩张至接近今日的规模；1974–75年德尔格废除君主制。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ethiopian Empire
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)
Bahru Zewde, A History of Modern Ethiopia, 1855–1991 (2nd ed., 2001)
Taddesse Tamrat, Church and State in Ethiopia 1270–1527 (1972)

note: Wikidata ends the empire in March 1975 (formal abolition of the monarchy); the emperor was deposed in September 1974. Tewodros and Yohannes were not of the Solomonic main line.

capital.zh: 达卡尔，后为哈勒尔（1520年起）

summary.en: A Muslim sultanate of the Horn of Africa, heir to Ifat, based in the Harar plateau and the Zeila trade route. Under Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim it nearly conquered Christian Ethiopia (1529–1543); weakened by war and Oromo migrations, it moved to Aussa in 1577.
summary.zh: 阿达尔是非洲之角的穆斯林苏丹国，继承伊法特，以哈勒尔高原和泽拉商路为根基。在伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣领导下几乎征服基督教埃塞俄比亚（1529–1543）；因战争和奥罗莫人迁徙而衰弱，1577年迁往奥萨。

name.zh: 伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐

sources.title: Wikipedia: Adal Sultanate
Shihab al-Din ʿArab Faqih, Futuh al-Habasha (c. 1559)
Richard Pankhurst, The Ethiopians: A History (1998)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. IV: Africa from the Twelfth to the Sixteenth Century (ed. D. T. Niane, 1984)

note: Capital coordinates are those of Harar; Wikidata places the sultanate further north-west.

summary.en: A Maliki reform movement of Sanhaja Berbers of the western Sahara, inspired by ʿAbdallah ibn Yasin, the Almoravids united Morocco, western Algeria and al-Andalus and controlled the gold trade with Ghana. They were overthrown by the Almohads, who took Marrakesh in 1147.
summary.zh: 穆拉比特王朝源于西撒哈拉桑哈贾柏柏尔人的马利克派改革运动，受阿卜杜拉·伊本·亚辛启发，统一摩洛哥、阿尔及利亚西部与安达卢斯，并控制与加纳的黄金贸易。1147年穆瓦希德攻占马拉喀什，王朝灭亡。

name.zh: 阿布·伯克尔·伊本·欧麦尔

sources.title: Wikipedia: Almoravid dynasty
Amira K. Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)
Ibn Abi Zarʿ, Rawd al-Qirtas (c. 1326)

note: Abu Bakr and Yusuf ruled jointly (Sahara and Maghreb respectively) from 1061.

summary.en: Founded on the doctrine of the Masmuda Berber reformer Ibn Tumart, the Almohads proclaimed a caliphate and for the first time united the whole Maghreb from the Atlantic to Tripolitania together with al-Andalus. Defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa (1212) began their decline.
summary.zh: 穆瓦希德王朝以马斯穆达柏柏尔改革者伊本·图迈尔特的教义为基础，自称哈里发，首次将从大西洋到的黎波里塔尼亚的整个马格里布与安达卢斯统一起来。1212年拉斯纳瓦斯德托洛萨之败后开始衰落。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Almohad Caliphate
Amira K. Bennison, The Almoravid and Almohad Empires (2016)
Britannica: Almohads

summary.en: Zenata Berbers who displaced the Almohads, the Marinids ruled Morocco from Fez, building madrasas such as the Bu ʿInaniyya. Abu al-Hasan briefly conquered Tlemcen and Tunis, and the court patronised Ibn Battuta and Ibn Khaldun.
summary.zh: 马林王朝出自取代穆瓦希德的扎纳塔柏柏尔人，以非斯为都统治摩洛哥，修建布伊纳尼亚等经学院。阿布·哈桑一度征服特莱姆森和突尼斯，宫廷曾庇护伊本·白图泰和伊本·赫勒敦。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Marinid dynasty
Maya Shatzmiller, The Berbers and the Islamic State: The Marinid Experience in Pre-Protectorate Morocco (2000)
Britannica: Marīnid dynasty

note: Wikidata gives 1215 (first Marinid incursions); 1244 is the usual start of the dynasty proper; Fez was taken in 1248.

summary.en: A sharifian dynasty from the Draa valley that led resistance to the Portuguese, the Saadis kept Morocco independent of the Ottomans. After Alcácer Quibir, Ahmad al-Mansur used ransom and sugar wealth to build the el-Badi palace and conquer Songhai.
summary.zh: 萨阿德王朝是来自德拉河谷的谢里夫王朝，领导抵抗葡萄牙人，使摩洛哥免于奥斯曼统治。阿尔卡塞尔基比尔战役后，艾哈迈德·曼苏尔凭借赎金和蔗糖财富修建巴迪宫并征服桑海。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Saadi Sultanate
Mercedes García-Arenal, Ahmad al-Mansur: The Beginnings of Modern Morocco (2009)
Britannica: Saʿdī dynasty

summary.en: The leading Swahili city-state of the medieval East African coast, Kilwa controlled the gold trade from Sofala, minted copper coins and built the Great Mosque and the Husuni Kubwa palace. Portuguese attacks from 1505 broke its power.
summary.zh: 基尔瓦是中世纪东非海岸首屈一指的斯瓦希里城邦，控制来自索法拉的黄金贸易，铸造铜币，修建大清真寺和胡苏尼库布瓦宫。1505年起葡萄牙人的攻击摧毁了其势力。

name.zh: 哈桑·伊本·苏莱曼（阿布·马瓦希卜）

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kilwa Sultanate
Kilwa Chronicle (Kitab al-Sulwa fi akhbar Kilwa)
H. Neville Chittick, Kilwa: An Islamic Trading City on the East African Coast (1974)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara

note: Founding date traditional (Kilwa Chronicle); the founder ʿAli ibn al-Hassan has no securely datable reign.

summary.en: Created by Usman dan Fodio’s jihad, the caliphate federated some thirty emirates across northern Nigeria and neighbouring lands under the sultan at Sokoto and the emir of Gwandu. It fostered extensive Islamic scholarship, including the writings of Nana Asmaʾu, before British conquest in 1903.
summary.zh: 索科托哈里发国由奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥的圣战建立，在索科托苏丹和关杜埃米尔之下联合尼日利亚北部及邻近地区约三十个酋长国。它孕育了丰富的伊斯兰学术，包括纳娜·阿斯玛的著作，1903年被英国征服。

name.zh: 穆罕默杜·阿塔希鲁一世

sources.title: Wikipedia: Sokoto Caliphate
Murray Last, The Sokoto Caliphate (1967)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)

summary.en: An Akan confederacy united around the Golden Stool under Osei Tutu, Asante became the dominant power of the forest zone of modern Ghana, trading gold, kola and captives. It fought a series of wars with Britain from 1824 to 1900 before annexation.
summary.zh: 阿散蒂是在奥塞·图图领导下以金凳子为核心联合起来的阿坎联盟，成为今加纳森林地带的霸主，从事黄金、可乐果与俘虏贸易。1824年至1900年间与英国多次交战，最终被吞并。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Asante Empire
Ivor Wilks, Asante in the Nineteenth Century (1975)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Asante Traditional Buildings
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. V: Africa from the Sixteenth to the Eighteenth Century (ed. B. A. Ogot, 1992)

note: Dates follow Wikidata (c. 1670 union; formal annexation 1902); independence from Denkyira dates from 1701. Osei Tutu’s accession date is uncertain (c. 1680–1695). Capital coordinates are Kumasi.

summary.en: A Fon kingdom on the Abomey plateau, Dahomey conquered the coastal ports of Allada and Ouidah in the 1720s and became a major participant in the Atlantic slave trade. It was renowned for its centralised administration and its female soldiers, and fell to France in 1892–94.
summary.zh: 达荷美是阿波美高原上的丰族王国，18世纪20年代征服沿海港口阿拉达和维达，成为大西洋奴隶贸易的重要参与者。它以中央集权的行政和女兵著称，1892–94年被法国征服。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Dahomey
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Royal Palaces of Abomey
Edna G. Bay, Wives of the Leopard: Gender, Politics, and Culture in the Kingdom of Dahomey (1998)
Robin Law, Ouidah: The Social History of a West African Slaving “Port”, 1727–1892 (2004)

note: Foundation date approximate (early 17th century).

summary.en: A Yoruba empire of the savanna north of the forest, Oyo built its power on cavalry and the trade between the coast and the Niger, holding Dahomey tributary for much of the 18th century. Internal revolt and the Sokoto jihad caused the abandonment of Oyo-Ile around 1835; a successor state survived at New Oyo.
summary.zh: 奥约是森林以北稀树草原上的约鲁巴帝国，以骑兵和沿海与尼日尔河之间的贸易为基础，18世纪大部分时间使达荷美纳贡。内乱与索科托圣战导致约1835年放弃奥约-伊莱，继承国在新奥约延续。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Oyo Empire
Robin Law, The Oyo Empire c. 1600–c. 1836 (1977)
Samuel Johnson, The History of the Yorubas (1921)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. V: Africa from the Sixteenth to the Eighteenth Century (ed. B. A. Ogot, 1992)

note: Origins are traditional; Wikidata ends the polity in 1905, after British conquest. Capital coordinates mark the Oyo-Ile (Old Oyo) ruins in Old Oyo National Park; Wikidata’s Oyo-Ile coordinates fall at modern Oyo town.

summary.en: The Edo kingdom ruled by the oba from Benin City, with vast earthworks and a guild-based court art in brass and ivory. Oba Ewuare expanded it in the 15th century, and it traded with the Portuguese from 1486. A British punitive expedition sacked the city in 1897 and looted the Benin Bronzes.
summary.zh: 贝宁王国是由奥巴在贝宁城统治的埃多人王国，拥有庞大的土墙工程和以行会为基础的黄铜、象牙宫廷艺术。15世纪奥巴埃瓦雷扩张国土，1486年起与葡萄牙人通商。1897年英国讨伐军洗劫该城并掠走贝宁青铜器。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Benin
Barbara Plankensteiner (ed.), Benin Kings and Rituals: Court Arts from Nigeria (2007)
Dan Hicks, The Brutish Museums: The Benin Bronzes, Colonial Violence and Cultural Restitution (2020)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. IV: Africa from the Twelfth to the Sixteenth Century (ed. D. T. Niane, 1984)

note: Disputed start: 1180 is the conventional date for Eweka I, first oba of the present dynasty (Egharevba’s chronology); Wikidata gives 1170, Britannica places Eweka in the 13th century, and the earlier Ogiso kingdom goes back to c. 900. Reigns before the 19th century are approximate.

capital.zh: 夸布拉瓦约，后为乌伦迪（翁迪尼）

summary.en: Forged by Shaka from the Zulu and neighbouring chiefdoms, the kingdom became the dominant power between the Drakensberg and the Indian Ocean. It defeated Britain at Isandlwana but was broken up after the war of 1879 and annexed to Natal in 1897.
summary.zh: 祖鲁王国由恰卡整合祖鲁及邻近酋邦而成，成为德拉肯斯山与印度洋之间的霸主。它在伊散德尔瓦纳击败英国，但1879年战后被肢解，1897年并入纳塔尔。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Zulu Kingdom
Jeff Guy, The Destruction of the Zulu Kingdom (1979)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)

summary.en: Founded by Muhammad Ahmad, who proclaimed himself the Mahdi in 1881 and drove out Turco-Egyptian rule, the state was governed from Omdurman by his successor, the Khalifa ʿAbdallahi. Anglo-Egyptian forces destroyed its army at Omdurman in 1898.
summary.zh: 马赫迪国家由1881年自称马赫迪并驱逐土耳其—埃及统治的穆罕默德·艾哈迈德建立，其继承人哈里发阿卜杜拉希以恩图曼为中心治国。1898年英埃联军在恩图曼摧毁其军队。

name.zh: 穆罕默德·艾哈迈德（马赫迪）

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mahdist State
P. M. Holt, The Mahdist State in the Sudan, 1881–1898 (1958)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VI: Africa in the Nineteenth Century until the 1880s (ed. J. F. Ade Ajayi, 1989)

summary.en: The state built by Samori Ture in the upper Niger basin, with a standing army, arms workshops and an Islamic administration. Fighting the French from 1882, it migrated eastward into present-day Côte d’Ivoire before Samori’s capture in 1898.
summary.zh: 瓦苏卢帝国是萨摩里·杜尔在尼日尔河上游建立的国家，拥有常备军、兵器作坊和伊斯兰行政体系。自1882年起与法国作战，后东迁至今科特迪瓦境内，1898年萨摩里被俘后灭亡。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Samorian State
Yves Person, Samori: une révolution dyula (1968–1975)
UNESCO General History of Africa, Vol. VII: Africa under Colonial Domination 1880–1935 (ed. A. Adu Boahen, 1985)

summary.en: The Nubian kingdom of Kush, which had once ruled Egypt as its 25th Dynasty, moved its royal centre south to Meroë around 300 BCE. Meroë smelted iron, wrote its own Meroitic script and buried its rulers in steep pyramids; queens called kandake often ruled in their own right. It declined in the 4th century CE.
summary.zh: 努比亚的库施王国曾作为第二十五王朝统治埃及，约公元前300年把王室中心南移至麦罗埃。麦罗埃冶铁，使用自己的麦罗埃文字，并以陡峭的金字塔安葬统治者；称为“坎达克”的女王常独立执政。公元4世纪王国衰落。

sources.title: László Török, The Kingdom of Kush: Handbook of the Napatan-Meroitic Civilization (1997)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe
Britannica: Kush
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Kush

note: Wikidata dates Kush from c. 1070 BCE (the end of Egyptian rule in Nubia). This record covers the Meroitic period only. Reign dates are approximate; Natakamani and Amanitore ruled jointly.

summary.en: Germanic Vandals and Alans crossed from Spain in 429 under Geiseric, were recognised by Rome in 435 and took Carthage in 439. Their kingdom, Arian Christian and with a powerful fleet, sacked Rome in 455 and persecuted the Catholic clergy at times, until Justinian’s general Belisarius conquered it in 533–534.
summary.zh: 日耳曼人汪达尔人和阿兰人在盖萨里克率领下于429年从西班牙渡海，435年获罗马承认，439年攻占迦太基。这个信奉阿里乌派基督教、拥有强大舰队的王国于455年洗劫罗马，并不时迫害天主教神职人员，直到533至534年被查士丁尼的将领贝利撒留征服。

sources.title: Andy Merrills and Richard Miles, The Vandals (2010)
Victor of Vita, History of the Vandal Persecution
Britannica: Vandal
Wikipedia: Vandal Kingdom

summary.en: Founded by Idris ibn Abdallah, a descendant of the Prophet’s grandson Hasan who fled the Abbasids after a failed revolt, the Idrisids were the first Islamic dynasty of Morocco. They founded Fez and spread Islam among the Berbers, but split into rival branches and were squeezed between the Fatimids and the Umayyads of Córdoba.
summary.zh: 伊德里斯王朝由先知外孙哈桑的后裔伊德里斯·本·阿卜杜拉创建，他在起义失败后逃离阿拔斯王朝。这是摩洛哥第一个伊斯兰王朝，建立了非斯并在柏柏尔人中传播伊斯兰教，但后来分裂为相互竞争的支系，夹在法蒂玛王朝与科尔多瓦倭马亚王朝之间。

sources.title: Hugh Kennedy, Muslim Spain and Portugal: A Political History of al-Andalus (1996)
Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed.: Idrisids
Britannica: Idrīsid dynasty
Wikipedia: Idrisid dynasty

note: Idris II ruled under a regent from his birth in 791 until 803. After 974 the last Idrisid briefly returned (985). Reign dates of later rulers vary between sources.

summary.en: Appointed by Harun al-Rashid, Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab and his heirs governed Ifriqiya as hereditary emirs under nominal Abbasid sovereignty. They built the Great Mosque of Kairouan and the ribats of the coast, conquered Sicily from 827 and fell to the Fatimid revolution in 909.
summary.zh: 受哈伦·拉希德任命，易卜拉欣·本·阿格拉布及其后代在阿拔斯王朝名义宗主权下世袭统治伊夫里基叶。他们修建了凯鲁万大清真寺和沿海的里巴特要塞，827年起征服西西里，909年亡于法蒂玛革命。

name.zh: 阿布·易卜拉欣·艾哈迈德

sources.title: Michael Brett, The Fatimid Empire (2017)
Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed.: Aghlabids
Britannica: Aghlabid dynasty
Wikipedia: Aghlabids

summary.en: A Sanhaja Berber family left to govern Ifriqiya when the Fatimids moved to Cairo in 972. Under al-Muʿizz ibn Badis the Zirids broke with Cairo, which loosed the Banu Hilal on them; confined to the coast at Mahdia, they fell to the Normans of Sicily in 1148.
summary.zh: 972年法蒂玛王朝迁往开罗时，留下这个桑哈贾柏柏尔家族治理伊夫里基叶。穆伊兹·本·巴迪斯时期齐里王朝与开罗决裂，开罗遂驱使巴努希拉勒进攻他们；他们被困于沿海的马赫迪耶，1148年亡于西西里诺曼人之手。

sources.title: Hady Roger Idris, La Berbérie orientale sous les Zīrīdes (1962)
Britannica: Zīrid dynasty
Wikipedia: Zirid dynasty

note: The Hammadid branch ruled the central Maghreb separately from 1015.

summary.en: The Hafsids, Almohad governors of Ifriqiya, declared independence in 1229 and made Tunis a Mediterranean capital of trade and learning, where Ibn Khaldun was born. Weakened by Spanish and Ottoman rivalry in the 16th century, the dynasty ended when the Ottomans took Tunis in 1574.
summary.zh: 哈夫斯家族原为穆瓦希德王朝的伊夫里基叶总督，1229年宣布独立，使突尼斯成为地中海贸易与学术之都，伊本·赫勒敦即生于此。16世纪在西班牙与奥斯曼的争夺中衰落，1574年奥斯曼攻占突尼斯，王朝终结。

name.zh: 阿布·扎卡里亚·叶海亚一世
阿布·叶海亚·阿布·伯克尔二世
阿布·阿拔斯·艾哈迈德二世
阿布·法里斯·阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹二世

sources.title: Robert Brunschvig, La Berbérie orientale sous les Hafsides (1940–47)
Britannica: Ḥafṣid dynasty
Wikipedia: Hafsid dynasty

summary.en: A Zenata family that served as viziers to the Marinids, the Wattasids took the throne of Fez in 1472. They ruled a shrinking northern Morocco while the Portuguese held the coast and the Saadians rose in the south, and were overthrown by the Saadians in 1554.
summary.zh: 瓦塔斯家族属泽纳塔柏柏尔人，曾任马林王朝的维齐尔，1472年在非斯登上王位。他们统治着日益缩小的摩洛哥北部，葡萄牙人占据海岸，萨阿德人在南方崛起；1554年被萨阿德王朝推翻。

sources.title: Abdallah Laroui, The History of the Maghrib: An Interpretive Essay (1977)
Britannica: Waṭṭāsid dynasty
Wikipedia: Wattasid dynasty

note: Members of the family were regents for the Marinids from 1420; their own sultanate dates from 1472.

capital.zh: 非斯、梅克内斯、马拉喀什；1912年起拉巴特

summary.en: Sharifs from the Tafilalt oasis claiming descent from the Prophet, the Alaouites took Fez in 1666 and reunited Morocco. They have reigned ever since, through the French and Spanish protectorates (1912–1956) and into the modern kingdom.
summary.zh: 阿拉维家族是来自塔菲拉勒特绿洲、自称先知后裔的谢里夫，1666年攻占非斯，重新统一摩洛哥。此后历经法国和西班牙保护国时期（1912—1956年），一直统治至今日的王国。

sources.title: C. R. Pennell, Morocco: From Empire to Independence (2003)
Britannica: ʿAlawite dynasty
Wikipedia: Alaouite dynasty

note: Al-Rashid’s brother Muhammad I had ruled the Tafilalt from 1631; the dynasty’s rule over Morocco dates from 1666. Mohammed V was exiled by France in 1953–55. “2025” means reigning today.

summary.en: The Funj sultanate succeeded the Christian kingdom of Alodia and ruled the middle Nile and the Gezira for three centuries. Its kings converted to Islam, and Sufi holy men spread the faith along the river; from 1761 the Hamaj regents held real power until the Egyptian conquest of 1821.
summary.zh: 芬吉苏丹国继基督教王国阿洛迪亚之后统治尼罗河中游和杰济拉地区达三个世纪。其国王皈依伊斯兰教，苏菲圣人沿河传播信仰；1761年起实权落入哈马吉摄政之手，直至1821年埃及征服。

name.zh: 穆罕默德·阿布·利凯利克（哈马吉摄政）

sources.title: Jay Spaulding, The Heroic Age in Sinnar (1985)
P. M. Holt and M. W. Daly, A History of the Sudan (6th ed., 2011)
Britannica: Funj Sultanate
Wikipedia: Funj Sultanate

note: Early dates follow the Funj Chronicle and are traditional.

summary.en: The Keira dynasty of the Fur ruled Darfur from the mid-17th century, controlling the Forty Days’ Road that carried captives, ivory and ostrich feathers to Egypt. Conquered by al-Zubayr and Egypt in 1874, it was restored by Ali Dinar in 1898 and annexed by Anglo-Egyptian Sudan in 1916.
summary.zh: 富尔人的凯拉王朝自17世纪中叶起统治达尔富尔，控制着把俘虏、象牙和鸵鸟羽毛运往埃及的“四十日之路”。1874年被祖拜尔和埃及征服，1898年由阿里·迪纳尔恢复，1916年被英埃苏丹吞并。

name.zh: 阿卜杜勒-拉赫曼·拉希德

sources.title: R. S. O’Fahey, The Darfur Sultanate: A History (2008)
Britannica: Darfur
Wikipedia: Sultanate of Darfur

note: Wikidata gives 1603; O’Fahey dates the Keira state to Sulayman Solongdungu, c. 1640s–1660. The sultanate was interrupted from 1874 to 1898.

summary.en: One of the Hausa city-states, Kano grew from a walled settlement around Dala hill into the greatest commercial city of the central Sudan, famous for its dyed cloth and leather. Its kings adopted Islam from the 14th century. Fulani jihadists overthrew the last Hausa king in 1807, and Kano became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate.
summary.zh: 卡诺是豪萨城邦之一，从达拉山周围有城墙的聚落发展为中苏丹最大的商业城市，以染布和皮革闻名。其国王自14世纪起接受伊斯兰教。1807年富拉尼圣战者推翻末代豪萨国王，卡诺成为索科托哈里发国的一个埃米尔国。

name.zh: 穆罕默德·阿尔瓦利二世

sources.title: The Kano Chronicle, trans. H. R. Palmer, Sudanese Memoirs vol. 3 (1928)
Murray Last, “Historical Metaphors in the Kano Chronicle”, History in Africa 7 (1980)
Britannica: Kano
Wikipedia: Kano

note: Early dates come from the Kano Chronicle (compiled c. 1890s) and are traditional; Bagauda is a legendary founder.

summary.en: An Mbundu kingdom between the Kwanza and Lukala rivers, ruled by kings with the title ngola, from which the name Angola comes. It resisted Portuguese conquest from Luanda for a century; Queen Njinga carried the struggle on from Matamba, and the Portuguese took the last stronghold, Pungo Andongo, in 1671.
summary.zh: 恩东戈是位于宽扎河与卢卡拉河之间的姆本杜王国，国王称号为“恩戈拉”，安哥拉之名即源于此。它从罗安达抵抗葡萄牙征服达一个世纪；女王恩津加在马坦巴继续斗争，1671年葡萄牙人攻占最后的据点蓬戈安东戈。

name.zh: 恩戈拉·基卢安杰·基亚·桑巴
恩戈拉·基卢安杰·基亚·恩丹比
姆班迪·恩戈拉·基卢安杰

sources.title: Linda M. Heywood, Njinga of Angola: Africa’s Warrior Queen (2017)
John K. Thornton, A History of West Central Africa to 1850 (2020)
Britannica: Ndongo
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Ndongo

note: The founding date is traditional. The site of Kabasa, near modern N’dalatando, is approximate. From 1626 the Portuguese installed client kings of the Hari line; the last, João Hari II, turned against them and fell when Pungo Andongo was taken in November 1671.

name.zh: 梅里纳王国（马达加斯加王国）

summary.en: The highland kingdom of Imerina was reunited by Andrianampoinimerina around 1790; his son Radama I, allied with Britain, extended it over most of Madagascar. Its 19th-century queens and prime ministers built a literate, partly Christian state, which France conquered in 1895 and abolished in 1897.
summary.zh: 高原王国伊默里纳约在1790年由安德里亚纳姆波伊尼梅里纳重新统一；其子拉达马一世与英国结盟，把统治扩展到马达加斯加大部分地区。19世纪的女王和首相们建立了一个有文字、部分基督教化的国家，1895年被法国征服，1897年被废除。

name.zh: 安德里亚纳姆波伊尼梅里纳

sources.title: Gwyn Campbell, An Economic History of Imperial Madagascar, 1750–1895 (2005)
Pier M. Larson, History and Memory in the Age of Enslavement: Becoming Merina in Highland Madagascar, 1770–1822 (2000)
Britannica: Merina
Wikipedia: Merina Kingdom

note: The early kings (Andriamanelo, c. 1540) are known from oral tradition; reign dates before 1787 are approximate.

summary.en: Separated from Oman on the death of Sayyid Said in 1856, the Busaidi sultanate ruled Zanzibar, Pemba and, nominally, the Swahili coast, growing rich on cloves, ivory and slaves. It became a British protectorate in 1890 and was overthrown by the Zanzibar Revolution a month after independence, in January 1964.
summary.zh: 1856年赛义德·赛义德去世后，布赛义德苏丹国从阿曼分离出来，统治桑给巴尔、奔巴并名义上统治斯瓦希里海岸，靠丁香、象牙和奴隶致富。1890年成为英国保护国，独立一个月后于1964年1月被桑给巴尔革命推翻。

sources.title: Abdul Sheriff, Slaves, Spices and Ivory in Zanzibar (1987)
Britannica: Zanzibar
Wikipedia: Sultanate of Zanzibar

summary.en: A kingdom on the north-western shore of Lake Victoria ruled by the kabaka, Buganda grew from a small state into the dominant power of the region by the 19th century, with a centralised chiefly administration and a fleet of war canoes. It became the core of the British Uganda Protectorate in 1894; the kingdom was abolished in 1966 and restored as a cultural institution in 1993.
summary.zh: 布干达是维多利亚湖西北岸由卡巴卡统治的王国，到19世纪已从小国发展为该地区的霸主，拥有中央集权的酋长行政体系和战船队。1894年成为英属乌干达保护国的核心；1966年王国被废除，1993年作为文化机构恢复。

sources.title: Richard J. Reid, Political Power in Pre-Colonial Buganda (2002)
M. S. M. Semakula Kiwanuka, A History of Buganda (1972)
Britannica: Buganda
Wikipedia: Buganda

note: The kingdom’s origins (14th–15th century) are known only from oral tradition. Mwanga II was briefly deposed in 1888–89.

name.en: Egypt under the Muhammad Ali dynasty
name.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里王朝治下的埃及

summary.en: Muhammad Ali’s descendants ruled Egypt as Ottoman governors, khedives (from 1867), sultans (1914) and kings (1922). They modernised the army, built railways and the Suez Canal, conquered Sudan and fell into debt and British occupation (1882). The Free Officers forced King Farouk out in 1952 and abolished the monarchy in 1953.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德·阿里的后代先后以奥斯曼总督、赫迪夫（1867年起）、苏丹（1914年）和国王（1922年）的身份统治埃及。他们推行军队现代化，修建铁路和苏伊士运河，征服苏丹，后陷入债务和英国占领（1882年）。1952年自由军官组织迫使法鲁克国王出走，1953年废除君主制。

sources.title: Khaled Fahmy, All the Pasha’s Men: Mehmed Ali, His Army and the Making of Modern Egypt (1997)
Afaf Lutfi al-Sayyid Marsot, A History of Egypt from the Arab Conquest to the Present (2nd ed., 2007)
Wikipedia: Muhammad Ali dynasty

note: Egypt remained formally part of the Ottoman Empire until 1914.

summary.en: A state in the Congo basin owned personally by King Leopold II of Belgium and recognised by the powers at the Berlin Conference. Its forced-labour regime for rubber and ivory caused mass death and an international reform campaign, and Belgium annexed it as the Belgian Congo in 1908.
summary.zh: 刚果自由邦是比利时国王利奥波德二世个人拥有、经柏林会议列强承认的刚果盆地国家。其为橡胶和象牙推行的强迫劳动制度造成大规模死亡，引发国际改革运动；1908年比利时将其吞并为比属刚果。

name.zh: 弗朗西斯·德温顿（行政长官）

sources.title: Adam Hochschild, King Leopold’s Ghost (1998)
Jean Stengers, Congo: Mythes et réalités (1989)
Britannica: Congo Free State
Wikipedia: Congo Free State

summary.en: The northernmost of the three Christian Nubian kingdoms, Nobatia arose between the First and Third Cataracts after the decline of Kush. Its king Silko left a victory inscription at Kalabsha, and a priest sent by Empress Theodora baptised its court in 543. Some time in the 7th century it was united with Makuria, keeping its own governor (eparch).
summary.zh: 诺巴迪亚是三个基督教努比亚王国中最北的一个，在库施衰落后兴起于尼罗河第一至第三瀑布之间。国王西尔科在卡拉布沙留下了战功铭文，543年狄奥多拉皇后派遣的教士为其宫廷施洗。7世纪某时它与马库里亚合并，但仍保留自己的总督（埃帕克）。

sources.title: Derek A. Welsby, The Medieval Kingdoms of Nubia (2002)
Artur Obłuski, The Rise of Nobadia: Social Changes in Northern Nubia in Late Antiquity (2014)
Wikipedia: Nobatia

note: Start (c. 400) and union with Makuria (7th century, certainly before 707) are approximate. Silko is dated only to around the mid-5th century; later kings such as Eirpanome (Dendur inscription, mid-6th century) have no reign dates.

summary.en: The southernmost Nubian kingdom, centred on the Gezira between the Blue and White Niles, Alodia was baptised by the bishop Longinus in 580. Arab geographers described its capital Soba as rich in churches and gardens. Weakened by Arab migration, it fell around 1500, and the Funj sultanate of Sennar rose in its place.
summary.zh: 阿勒底亚是最南的努比亚王国，以青尼罗河与白尼罗河之间的杰济拉为中心，580年由主教隆吉努斯施洗皈依。阿拉伯地理学家称其都城索巴教堂林立、园林繁茂。王国因阿拉伯部落迁入而衰弱，约1500年灭亡，芬吉人的森纳尔苏丹国随之兴起。

name.zh: 摩西·乔治（兼马库里亚国王）

sources.title: Derek A. Welsby, The Medieval Kingdoms of Nubia (2002)
Mohi el-Din Abdalla Zarroug, The Kingdom of Alwa (1991)
Wikipedia: Alodia

note: Alodia is first mentioned in 569 and probably formed earlier. Its fall (c. 1500–1504) is credited by the Funj Chronicle to Amara Dunqas and by most modern scholars to the Abdallab Arabs. Reign dates are approximate.

summary.en: A Saharan people of the Fezzan in south-western Libya who built walled towns and watered oases through foggaras, hand-dug tunnels tapping fossil groundwater. They traded and fought with Rome, whose armies reached Garama but never ruled the Fezzan. Their state declined as the water ran down and had faded by the 7th century.
summary.zh: 加拉曼特人是利比亚西南部费赞地区的撒哈拉民族，修筑有城墙的城镇，并开凿名为“福加拉”的地下暗渠汲取化石地下水灌溉绿洲。他们与罗马既通商又交战，罗马军队曾抵达加拉马，却从未统治费赞。随着地下水枯竭，其国家逐渐衰落，到7世纪已不复存在。

sources.title: David J. Mattingly (ed.), The Archaeology of Fazzan, vol. 1: Synthesis (2003)
Britannica: Garamantes
Wikipedia: Garamantes

note: Dates are approximate: Garamantian settlement goes back to c. 1000 BCE and a polity controlling the oases is usually dated from the mid-1st millennium BCE to the late 7th century CE. No rulers are known by name. The Wikidata item is the people.

summary.en: The sacred city of the Yoruba, where tradition places the creation of the world and the first kingship under Oduduwa. Between about 1000 and the early 15th century Ife was a walled city of glass-bead workshops and potsherd pavements whose artists cast the famous copper-alloy heads. Later eclipsed by Oyo and Benin, its Ooni remains the most senior Yoruba king.
summary.zh: 伊费是约鲁巴人的圣城，传说世界在此创生，奥杜杜瓦在此开创最早的王权。约1000年至15世纪初，伊费是一座筑有城墙的城市，有玻璃珠作坊和陶片铺地，其工匠铸造了著名的铜合金头像。后来伊费被奥约和贝宁所超越，但其国王“奥尼”至今仍是地位最尊的约鲁巴君主。

sources.title: Akinwumi Ogundiran, The Yoruba: A New History (2020)
Suzanne Preston Blier, Art and Risk in Ancient Yoruba: Ife History, Power, and Identity, c. 1300 (2015)
Wikipedia: Ife Empire

note: The span covers Ife’s classical period of urban growth and art (c. 1000–1420, after Ogundiran); the Ooni’s kingdom continued afterwards. Early Oonis, including Oduduwa, are known only from tradition, so no reign dates are given.

capital.en: Royal towns near Kabongo (moved each reign)
capital.zh: 卡邦戈一带的王城（每代国王迁移）

summary.en: A kingdom of the Upemba depression in south-eastern Congo, ruled by a sacred king (mulopwe) whose authority rested on the founding epic of Nkongolo and Kalala Ilunga, recited with the help of beaded memory boards (lukasa). It expanded in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, then broke apart under raids by East African ivory and slave traders and a succession war in the 1880s.
summary.zh: 卢巴是刚果东南部乌彭巴洼地的王国，由神圣君主“穆洛普韦”统治，其权威来自恩孔戈洛与卡拉拉·伊隆加的建国史诗，史诗借助缀珠的记忆板“卢卡萨”诵述。王国在18世纪末至19世纪初扩张，后因东非象牙和奴隶商人的劫掠以及19世纪80年代的王位之争而分裂。

name.en: Kalala Ilunga (legendary founder of the dynasty)
name.zh: 卡拉拉·伊隆加（传说中的王朝开创者）

sources.title: Thomas Q. Reefe, The Rainbow and the Kings: A History of the Luba Empire to 1891 (1981)
John Stewart, African States and Rulers, 3rd ed. (2006)
Mary Nooter Roberts and Allen F. Roberts, Memory: Luba Art and the Making of History (1996)
Wikipedia: Luba Empire

note: The origin is disputed: Congolese historians date the traditions as early as the 8th–15th centuries, Reefe the state to the 17th–18th. The 1585 start and all reign dates follow Stewart and are approximate; Nkongolo and Kalala Ilunga are figures of the founding epic. The kingdom split in 1889 and was absorbed by the Congo Free State.

summary.en: A kingdom of the southern Congo savanna whose rulers took the title Mwaant Yav (Mwata Yamvo). Tradition traces it to the marriage of the Lunda ruler Lueji and the Luba hunter Chibinda Ilunga. From the late 17th century it sent out chiefs who founded tributary kingdoms as far as the Kwango and the Luapula, and sold slaves and ivory towards the Atlantic. Chokwe invaders overran its capital in 1887.
summary.zh: 隆达是刚果南部稀树草原上的王国，其君主称“姆瓦安特·亚夫”（姆瓦塔·亚姆沃）。传说它源于隆达女首领卢埃吉与卢巴猎人奇宾达·伊隆加的联姻。17世纪末起，它派出首领在远至宽果河和卢阿普拉河的地方建立朝贡王国，并向大西洋沿岸输出奴隶和象牙。1887年乔奎人攻占其都城。

sources.title: Jan Vansina, Kingdoms of the Savanna (1966)
John K. Thornton, A History of West Central Africa to 1850 (2020)
Wikipedia: Lunda Empire

note: The Mwaant Yav title is traditionally dated to c. 1665, and Nawej (c. 1695) is the first well-attested ruler; reign dates are too uncertain to list. The end date is the Chokwe capture of the Musumba; the heartland was partitioned between Angola, the Congo Free State and British Rhodesia from 1884–1891.
